correctness.rationale: The last-reset age A is exponential, and first reset couples any initial distributions, giving a unique stationary law. At age A the damped reset noise and subsequent OU noise have total variance V exp(−2κA)+V(1−exp(−2κA))=V; the resulting Gaussian is independent in distribution of age and sign. exp(−κA) has density a u^(a−1) on (0,1), giving the stated dimensionless convolution. For 0<a≤1 a layer-cake decomposition into centered uniforms gives a strictly negative derivative on the positive half-line after Gaussian convolution. For a>1 the derivative of the input has an interior signed power and jumps of magnitude a/2 at the endpoints. Convolving gives the stated positive prefactor times H_{a,t}(w)−1. The ratio sinh(uw)/sinh(w) strictly decreases in w for 0<u<1 by monotonicity of z coth z, and goes from u to zero. This gives exactly the claimed derivative signs at all positive positions. H_a(0)=1−1/a, H'_a(t)>0, and H_a tends to infinity as t increases, so the unique critical t exists and strictly separates the modes. At t_c the Taylor coefficient in w² is −H'_a(t_c)/6, and the positive prefactor vanishes linearly in w: the stationary density has zero second and negative fourth derivative at the center. The positive root approaches zero by monotonicity and continuity of the sign kernel; its equation expanded in w² yields w²=6(t−t_c)+o(t−t_c). Since w is dimensionless position divided by s, m²=3(s_c−s)+o(s_c−s). H_2(t)=(exp(t)−1)/(2t) gives the numerical root (independently checked). The bound H_a(t)≤(a−1)exp(t)/a proves divergence of t_c as a decreases to one; for U~Beta(a,1), E[1−U²]=2/(a+2) and E[(1−U²)²]=8/((a+2)(a+4)), giving a(H_a(t)−1)→2t−1 locally uniformly and t_c→1/2. Finite quadratures are only corroboration.
residual_risks: Quoted finite quadrature and exact-relation root differ by about 1.36×10^-9, within the supporting numerical tolerances. Gaussian variance must equal D/κ and weights must be equal; replacing packets with atoms changes the result.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The renewal integral is not itself a mode theorem. evidence: The mathematical formulation is the Gaussian smoothing of a symmetric compact power density. Sabhapandit–Majumdar smooth (1−u²)^(ν−1), which is positive at zero for all admissible ν; the reset input for a>1 vanishes there. The assigned Resultary record itself is not a distinct hit.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The power-smoothing formulation is a true equivalent and needs the same prior-art test. After normalization to the common support [-1,1], these two compact densities differ on neighborhoods of the center, not just at a single density version point; Gaussian smoothing is injective at the same variance by its nonvanishing Fourier multiplier. Thus the prior active-particle threshold is not the same family in another notation.

originality.rationale: Last-reset renewal, one-dimensional Gaussian smoothing, curvature-zero mode boundaries in related models, and coefficient 3 in the analogous run-and-tumble bifurcation are established. The distinct result is the global mode classification and explicit threshold for complete equal thermal-packet resets: its compact input is the symmetric truncated power |u|^(a−1), not the compact telegraph Beta profile or an age-dependent-width point-reset law. The checked primary run-and-tumble work is an important additional comparison beyond the cited resetting papers.
residual_risks: A prior equivalent classification under critical bandwidth or Gaussian smoothing of monotone compact power profiles is not exhaustively excluded. The inspected evidence supports the specific threshold and complete mode count, not priority for renewal, generic quartic heat-flow expansions or the coefficient 3 alone.

value.rationale: Thermal-width packet resetting is a natural parameter calibration that retains a diffusive bath while making the smearing exact. The result shows that rate alone is insufficient above a=1, gives the precise thermal variance at which distinct maxima disappear, and rules out further peaks globally. This matters when interpreting a reset-induced change in the stationary density, and distinguishes it from the flat transition of idealized point targets, rather than just evaluating a known moment or a generic local coefficient.
residual_risks: No extension to unequal packets, age-dependent post-reset variance, transient modes, or the physical cost of preparation is established.
